refinement.detail: Searched, found nothing to apply. PA-03's implementation_scope is [scripts/generate_cases_from_tlc_dump.py, prompts/hexagonal_implementation.md, references/generation_modes.md, tests/] and its conflict_keys.tla is EMPTY, so there is no modeled representation in scope to refine -- measured delta direction=zero, and the ticket's declared model_delta_expectation was "possibly one generation-mode variant". One was added and it carries ZERO model delta, stated before the flag was written and now measured: `effects` is a DECLARATION TABLE, not TLA+ state. No variable, no action, no Next disjunct, no CONSTANT. TLC explores the identical state graph before and after -- 6,223 states from MCsmall.cfg either way -- so max_distinct_states and max_state_space_bound are untouched and the predecessor's measured ~8x state-space cost per surface-adding ticket does not apply. ONE REFINEMENT WAS AVAILABLE AND WAS DELIBERATELY REFUSED, and it is the interesting one. A port's REGION could have been declared in the manifest as a `writes:` key beside the port, which is simpler to implement and would let a port name a region the model does not support. It was refused under declaration_executability_rule: it is a second declaration of a fact the model already carries, and its failure mode is that the declared region and the action write sets drift with nothing able to notice. Deriving the region from written_variables -- the same function the negative corpus uses to choose what it may negate -- means the declaration cannot be WRONG about the model, only DISAGREE with it, and the disagreement is counted and printed every run in both directions. The one measurable complexity cost is corpus size, and it went DOWN on every corpus it was run beside: 43,128 -> 1,855 on the A/B fixture (23x), 99,817 -> 29,921 on this repository's own model with 15 declared ports. The flag is off by default, so no existing corpus moves at all.

kill_rate.evidence: The MF-016 kill-test harness over specs/current/kill_mutants.toml was not run. A DIFFERENT and much larger kill measurement WAS run and is the ticket's product: the A/B catalogue, per class and per arm, over eight instruments on both sealed EVAL-RERUN arms, with executable counts beside every number -- specs/tickets/PA-03/results/kill-table-arm-{a,b}.json. Recorded as `not_run` because it is not the member this field names, and collapsing the two would be exactly the kind of substitution the ledger asks about.

ticket.model_delta_expectation: Possibly one generation-mode variant. Per surface_cost_rule, state what it buys and what the state space costs BEFORE adding it -- the predecessor measured ~1.5 new coverage gaps and ~8x state space per surface-adding ticket.
ticket.objective: The first half of making the two senses of "adapter" one object. The prompt already makes an agent declare ports in the DOMAIN'S vocabulary. Have it declare them in the MANIFEST too, in the same shape the toolchain already uses for effect ports -- so a port the agent invented becomes a port the toolchain knows about. Then generate cases PER PORT, not only per action. Today every generated case drives a whole action, which is why a hexagonal codebase and a non-hexagonal one produce identical verdicts on 49 of 49 comparable cells: the port boundary is invisible to generation. NOTE, added by the epic owner 2026-08-05: 49 of 49 is the SEALED HP-06 number and it was SUPERSEDED before this epic opened. EVAL-RERUN at b3a0199 replicated and widened it to 56 OF 56 strictly comparable cells on a fresh artifact pair and a wider catalogue. Aim at 56 of 56. See GOAL-cases-drive-ports.baseline for why the bar moved up. Inherit rather than rebuild. The negative-corpus mode already emits the disabled edges at each reachable state and took guard relaxation from 0 of 3 to 3 of 3; per-port generation should compose with it, not replace it. And the tractability work stands: a corpus nobody can run is not a mechanism, and this model needed a projection to produce one at all.
